Satellite Communications Resellers & Integrators across Starlink, OneWeb, Viasat and SES

LEO SatelliteMarket AnalysisFinancialEutelsat OneWeb

Profiles of 13 satcom resellers and integrators spanning Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, Viasat/Inmarsat and SES/Intelsat channels: Marlink, Speedcast, KVH, Gogo (incl. Satcom Direct), Panasonic Avionics, Hughes, Navarino, Network Innovations, Tampnet, Space Norway, Nelco, Telstra and Kymeta. It covers ownership, financials where public, sector focus (maritime, aviation, enterprise, government) and documented operator relationships, and notes Starlink’s May 2026 freeze on new reseller applications.

Satellite Communications Resellers & Integrators: Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, Viasat/Inmarsat and SES/Intelsat

Financials, business sectors and capabilities of the leading channel partners — research report as of 4 November 2026

Prepared for: Paul | Date: 4 November 2026 | Coverage: developments through 4 Nov 2026

Note on sources: in-text citations [n] are clickable links to the primary or trade-press source; full numbered references with access notes are at the end. 'n.v.' = not verified; 'n.d.' = not disclosed; 'Hist.' = historic relationship.

1. Executive summary

The satcom channel has been reshaped since 2024 by three forces: Starlink's scale (SpaceX's Connectivity segment, driven primarily by Starlink, generated $11,387m of revenue in FY2025, up 49.8% [1]), the consolidation of GEO/MEO operators (SES closed its acquisition of Intelsat on 17 July 2025 [2]; Viasat now owns Inmarsat), and the rise of multi-orbit managed services, in which resellers bundle two or more networks under one SLA and one contract.

This report profiles 13 resellers, distribution partners and integrators chosen for their scale, how many of the four operators they work with, and their importance to particular sectors. The private-equity-owned maritime/energy managed-service providers (Marlink, Speedcast, Navarino) and listed specialists (KVH, Gogo) are the most visible, while integrators such as Hughes, Panasonic Avionics, Telstra and Space Norway serve as distribution channels in aviation, telecom backhaul and regional markets.

Key takeaways

  • Marlink is the largest independent multi-orbit integrator. It reports annual revenues of more than $800m [3]. It runs Starlink and OneWeb as managed LEO layers under a single data allowance (Sealink Multi-LEO, launched March 2026) [3], has an O3b mPOWER commitment with SES [4], won a 300+-vessel OneWeb deployment for CMA CGM [5], and refinanced its $670m and €378m term loans in August 2026 [6].
  • Speedcast has become an asset-light, LEO-centric integrator. It is a Tier 1 Authorized Starlink Integrator with more than 18,000 Starlink kits sold [7] and a OneWeb Global Distribution Partner [8]. On 3 November 2026 it completed the sale of 12 teleports to EQT-backed SatPort and leased the capacity back under a long-term agreement [9]. It does not publish revenue; one third-party estimate puts 2024 revenue at about $500m [10] (unverified).
  • The listed resellers are being repriced around LEO. KVH's FY2025 revenue was $111.0m (down 2%), but LEO/HTS airtime made up 82% of net sales [11], and Q2 2026 revenue rose 27% year on year on Starlink and OneWeb subscriber growth [12]. Gogo's FY2025 revenue was $910.5m after the Satcom Direct acquisition [13], but Moody's cut it to B2 in January 2026, citing competition, including a lost NetJets opportunity to Starlink, and 4.4x pro-forma leverage [14].
  • Starlink's channel is tightening, not disappearing. In May 2026 SpaceX paused new authorized-reseller applications, saying indirect deals should be reserved for 'truly strategic opportunities' (licensing, language, operational reach, regulated markets) [15]. Its S-1 says channel partners in select geographies will help drive enterprise and government adoption [1]. Incumbent Tier 1 integrators gain scarcity value, while smaller resellers face disintermediation.
  • OneWeb and SES depend more on partners. Eutelsat's LEO revenue rose 69.5% like-for-like to €297m in FY2025-26 (25% of group revenue), helped by distribution partners including SES and the newly signed Tototheo [16]. SES (pro-forma net leverage 4.4x at H1 2026 against a ≤3.0x target [17]) needs its partner programme [18] and its own multi-orbit products, including a MEO-plus-Starlink cruise service [19], to defend share.
  • Consolidation continues. Recent deals include Viasat's $203m exit from Navarino to ICG [20], Network Innovations' purchase of Telesat's Infosat [21], Marlink's agreed acquisition of UK defence integrator GRC [22], Platinum Equity's purchase of Anuvu [23], and Speedcast's teleport carve-out [9]. Expect more PE-to-PE trades, infrastructure carve-outs and defence-led bolt-ons in 2026-2028.

Scope, selection criteria and method

Selection criteria. Candidates were screened on: (1) the number of the four operators (Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, Viasat/Inmarsat, SES/Intelsat) with which a documented reseller, distribution or capacity relationship exists; (2) scale (revenue, installed terminals/vessels/aircraft); (3) importance in at least one key vertical (maritime, energy, aviation, government/defence, enterprise, telecom backhaul/consumer); and (4) availability of verifiable sources. Operators themselves (Telesat, Viasat Government, SES's own direct sales) are excluded as profiles but discussed in the market overview. Candidates from the brief that were not profiled (e.g., Castor Marine, OmniAccess, BlueSky Network, Satcom Global, Clarus, Comtech, ST Engineering iDirect, NTT, BT, Orange, Vodafone, AT&T, Verizon, Hanwha Systems, Ultisat) were omitted for scale, because they are primarily equipment vendors, or because time constraints prevented primary-source verification of their operator relationships. Ultisat is covered within Speedcast, which owns it [24].

Evidence rules. Every figure is tied to a source and fiscal period. Relationships are marked Yes only where an operator, the company or a filing states them. Historic or unconfirmed relationships are labelled. For private companies, company-stated or third-party figures are flagged as such. All URLs were checked with curl (following redirects) on 4 Nov 2026; access notes are given in the References.

2. Market overview: how reselling works for each operator

Starlink (SpaceX)

Model. Starlink is mainly sold directly to consumers. SpaceX says consumer subscribers were over 60% of Connectivity segment revenue in 2025, and its 10.3m 'Starlink Subscribers' figure excludes managed enterprise and government contracts in aviation, maritime, land mobility, fixed sites and government [1,25]. Enterprise sales run through specialised direct sales teams plus a channel of authorized resellers and integrators. Speedcast and KVH describe themselves as 'Tier 1' authorized resellers [7,11], and premium products such as Global High Throughput and Private Network Interconnect are offered through 'a limited set of authorized Starlink integrators' [26].

Maritime and aviation. Maritime service is sold both directly and through resellers [27]. Business aviation uses OEMs and authorized dealer/installers listed on Starlink's aviation page [28], and airline deals are largely negotiated directly. That leaves little room for classic resellers in aviation.

2026 shift. Starlink paused new authorized-reseller applications in May 2026, citing 'overwhelming' demand, compliance risk and reduced visibility into end customers. PCMag reports a network of about 200 resellers and a former guideline that applicants should target at least $5m of annual recurring revenue [15]; see also Quilty's analysis [29]. At the same time, SpaceX's S-1 (May 2026) says it will expand 'through channel partners in select geographies' for enterprise and government [1], and CRN reports IT solution providers such as CDW, Insight and WWT among North American partners [30]. SpaceX priced its IPO on 11 June 2026 [31]. CNBC reports proceeds of $85.7bn including the over-allotment [32].

Eutelsat OneWeb

Model. OneWeb is a wholesale/B2B network with no direct-to-consumer offer. Service reaches end users through distribution partners (DPs) such as Speedcast, Kymeta, Hughes and Network Innovations [33,34,35], through national partners (e.g., Nelco in India [36]), and through direct sovereign contracts (e.g., the French DGA CENTAURE call-off under the €1bn NEXUS framework) [16].

Momentum. In FY2025-26 (year to 30 June 2026), LEO revenue reached €297.0m, up 69.5% like-for-like, out of group revenue of €1,235.9m and Adjusted EBITDA of €632.4m. Net debt/EBITDA fell to 2.32x after a €5bn refinancing [16]. Eutelsat calls SES 'Eutelsat's distribution partner' in aviation (JAL, LATAM) and signed new maritime partners Tototheo and AST Networks [16].

Viasat (incl. Inmarsat)

Model. Inmarsat services are sold through independent partners and value-added resellers worldwide, which can be found in a searchable partner directory [37,38]. Viasat also sells directly to airlines and governments. In maritime, the multi-orbit NexusWave product (bonded Ka GEO, LEO, LTE and L-band) is sold through resellers and partners [39].

Financials. Viasat's FY2026 (to 31 March 2026) revenue was $4.6bn and Adjusted EBITDA $1.6bn, both records. Net debt fell to $4.8bn after repaying the remaining $300m Inmarsat term loan [20]. Aviation grew at a double-digit rate, while fixed residential and maritime declined. NexusWave ended the year with 1,350 vessels in service and 1,500 on order [20]. Viasat sold its minority stake in distribution partner Navarino to an ICG subsidiary for $203m and kept a commercial relationship [20].

SES (incl. O3b mPOWER and Intelsat)

Intelsat deal completed. SES closed the Intelsat acquisition on 17 July 2025 for $2.6bn (€2.2bn) in cash plus contingent value rights [2,40]. The combined fleet has about 90 GEO and nearly 30 MEO satellites [2]. Intelsat therefore no longer acts as an independent buyer or reseller. Its aviation business, including the network-sharing arrangement with Gogo and the OneWeb aviation distribution role, now sits within SES [41,16].

Channel. The SES partner programme covers value-added solution providers, authorized resellers, integrators and telcos, with tiered benefits [18]. SES also sells direct, notably the 'Cruise mPOWERED + Starlink' integrated MEO-LEO service [19], which makes SES both a supplier and a competitor to cruise-focused resellers.

Financials. FY2025 reported revenue was €2,627m and Adjusted EBITDA €1,196m (like-for-like €3,512m and €1,529m), with like-for-like net leverage of 3.9x [42]. H1 2026 revenue was €1,602m (like-for-like −5.0%), and Adjusted Net Debt/Adjusted EBITDA was 4.4x against a target of ≤3.0x [17].

3. Reseller and integrator profiles

1. Marlink

Ownership / HQ

Private equity: Providence Equity Partners (majority since July 2022), with Apax, Ardian and management as minority holders [43]. HQ Paris and Oslo [43].

Operators

Starlink – Yes [3,44,30]; OneWeb – Yes [5]; Viasat/Inmarsat – historic Fleet Xpress alliance (2016) [45], current status not verified; SES – Yes, O3b mPOWER [4].

Sectors

Maritime, energy, enterprise, government/defence, humanitarian [43,22].

Capabilities

Multi-orbit managed network (LEO/MEO/GEO + cellular) with SD-WAN traffic steering, XChange NextGen edge platform, Marlink Cyber, IT/cloud [5,3].

Financials

Annual revenue 'surpassing $800 million', 1,500 employees (company statement, Mar 2026; fiscal year not specified) [3]. Valued at $1.4bn in the 2021 Providence deal [46]. Financing: refinanced $670m and €378m term B facilities and amended its $140m RCF (Aug 2026) [6]. S&P rates the Venga Holdings borrowing group [47], but the rating level could not be verified (page blocked).

Key 2026 developments: Sealink Multi-LEO, a single managed data allowance across Starlink and OneWeb (500 GB–10 TB, fleet pooling) [3]; a multi-year CMA CGM deal to deploy OneWeb on more than 300 vessels within nine months [5]; and a definitive agreement (11 Aug 2026) to acquire UK defence integrator GRC, which contributes about £35m of revenue [22]. Completion of the GRC deal was expected 'later in August 2026' but was not independently confirmed for this report.

2. Speedcast

Ownership / HQ

Private equity: Centerbridge Partners, owner since March 2021 [9]. HQ Houston, Texas [9].

Operators

Starlink – Yes, Tier 1 Authorized Integrator/Reseller [7]; OneWeb – Yes, Global Distribution Partner [8]; Viasat/Inmarsat – limited: sold its Inmarsat maritime reseller base back to Inmarsat during its 2020-21 restructuring and continues to resell Inmarsat-C GMDSS [10] (third-party account); SES – historic O3b MEO agreements (e.g., Peru, 2017) [48].

Sectors

Maritime (merchant, cruise), offshore and land energy, government (via UltiSat), enterprise/telecom [10,24].

Capabilities

SIGMA intelligent-edge/SD-WAN platform; field engineering (110+ engineers across six continents); first to market with Starlink HTS and PNI services [7,26]; serves more than 3,200 customers in more than 140 countries [9].

Financials

Private; revenue not disclosed. Valour Consultancy estimates 2024 revenue at about $500m (third-party estimate, unverified) [10]. In May 2025 Bloomberg reported that Speedcast was considering a sale of its ground-station business for more than $1bn [49] (paywalled). The teleport sale (12 teleports in 11 countries) to SatPort/EQT completed on 3 Nov 2026; deal value not disclosed [9].

Speedcast has moved from a GEO-VSAT network owner to an asset-light LEO integrator. It sold more than 10,000 Starlink kits by November 2024 [24] and more than 18,000 by 2026 [7]. Hughes resells Starlink to US enterprises through a partnership with Speedcast [50], showing that Speedcast also acts as a wholesale integrator for other channels.

3. KVH Industries

Ownership / HQ

Public (Nasdaq: KVHI). HQ Bristol, Rhode Island [12].

Operators

Starlink – Yes, 'Starlink Authorized Tier 1 reseller' [11]; OneWeb – Yes, authorized reseller [11]; Viasat/Inmarsat – Inmarsat services included in KVH ONE [11]; SES – Yes, Ku-band VSAT over the SES HTS network [11].

Sectors

Maritime (commercial, leisure, fishing), plus land/inland waterways via Starlink Local Priority [11].

Capabilities

KVH ONE hybrid network (satellite + 5G/LTE + Wi-Fi), TracNet hybrid terminals, CommBox Edge, the KVH Manager/myKVH portals, and content services [11].

Financials

FY2025: revenue $111.0m (−2%); service revenue $98.4m (+2%); net loss $7.4m; Adjusted EBITDA $8.1m [51]. LEO/HTS airtime was 82% of net sales [11]. No interest expense was reported for 2025 [51]. Q2 2026: revenue $33.7m (+27% YoY), airtime revenue $27.8m (+31%) on Starlink and OneWeb subscriber growth, Adjusted EBITDA $3.0m [12].

KVH is the clearest public 'pure-play' on maritime LEO resale. It has accepted lower product margins and the loss of legacy VSAT revenue to win recurring Starlink and OneWeb airtime. Given its small scale, its main risk is margin pressure from Starlink pricing and Starlink's direct maritime plans.

4. Gogo (incl. Satcom Direct)

Ownership / HQ

Public (Nasdaq: GOGO). HQ Broomfield, Colorado [13]. Acquired Satcom Direct on 3 Dec 2024 [13,52].

Operators

Starlink – No (competitor) [14]; OneWeb – Yes, Gogo Galileo on the Eutelsat OneWeb network [41,53]; Viasat/Inmarsat – Yes, GEO services incl. Jet ConneX (Satcom Direct has been a Level 1 VAR since 2018) [41,54]; SES (incl. Intelsat) – Yes, GEO services plus an ATG network-sharing agreement with Intelsat (now SES) [41].

Sectors

Business aviation; military/government aviation [13].

Capabilities

Describes itself as the only multi-orbit, multi-band business-aviation provider, combining ATG (incl. Gogo 5G, launched Jan 2026), GEO Ku/Ka and LEO (Galileo with a Hughes-designed ESA); approximately 8,050 customers [41,13].

Financials

FY2025: revenue $910.5m (+105%; pro-forma +1.5%); Adjusted EBITDA $217.8m; net income $12.9m; free cash flow $89.2m [13]. Total debt $848.3m at 31 Dec 2025 [41]. 2026 guidance: revenue $905–945m, Adjusted EBITDA $198–218m [13]. Moody's downgraded Gogo to B2 (stable) on 27 Jan 2026, citing pro-forma debt/EBITDA of 4.4x [14].

Gogo is the leading multi-operator channel in business aviation, but it is the most exposed to Starlink, which competes directly with OEM/dealer distribution [28]. Q3 2026 results are due on 6 Nov 2026 and were not available for this report.

5. Panasonic Avionics

Ownership / HQ

Wholly owned Panasonic Group subsidiary, reported within the Panasonic Connect segment [55].

Operators

Starlink – No; OneWeb – Yes, LEO provider for its multi-orbit network [56,57]; Viasat/Inmarsat – not verified; SES (incl. Intelsat) – Panasonic says it uses 'GEO satellite operators' without naming them in the cited release [56], so not confirmed here.

Sectors

Commercial aviation inflight entertainment and connectivity (IFEC).

Capabilities

Multi-orbit IFC network with in-flight LEO/GEO switching (validated in April 2025), antenna partnerships, and cabin/IFE integration [56].

Financials

Avionics revenue is not disclosed separately. Panasonic Connect segment sales were ¥1,380.3bn in FY2026 (to March 2026), and Avionics is cited as a growth driver [55].

Panasonic is an integrator that resells capacity under its own SLA to airlines. Eutelsat OneWeb is its LEO partner.

6. Hughes Network Systems (EchoStar)

Ownership / HQ

Subsidiary of EchoStar Corp. (Nasdaq: SATS) [58].

Operators

Starlink – Yes, Starlink service for enterprise via a partnership with Speedcast [50]; OneWeb – Yes, global distribution partner [34,50] and Galileo ESA co-designer [41]; Viasat/Inmarsat – not verified; SES – not verified.

Sectors

Consumer satellite broadband (HughesNet), enterprise/SD-WAN, government/defence, aviation.

Capabilities

JUPITER GEO HTS fleet, managed LEO, multi-transport SD-WAN/SASE, OneWeb ESAs [50].

Financials

EchoStar's Broadband & Satellite Services segment: FY2025 revenue $1,456.1m (2024: $1,575.8m); Adjusted OIBDA $327.2m; 739,000 broadband subscribers [58]. EchoStar group net loss of $14.50bn, driven by about $17.63bn of non-cash impairments [58]. In 2025 EchoStar agreed to sell spectrum to SpaceX [59]; Reuters valued the deal at about $17bn [60].

Hughes is unusual in being an operator, a OneWeb distribution partner and, through Speedcast, a Starlink channel. Its relationship with SpaceX deepened through the 2025 spectrum transaction [59].

7. Navarino

Ownership / HQ

Private: founders with ICG (European Corporate), following ICG's purchase of Viasat's minority stake [61,62,20]. UK and Greece; 15 hubs [61].

Operators

Starlink – Yes; OneWeb – Yes; Viasat/Inmarsat – Yes (Fleet Xpress, NexusWave, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C); SES – not verified. All per Navarino's own product listings [61].

Sectors

Merchant maritime.

Capabilities

COSMO connectivity/security management platform, IT and cloud (Infinity), cyber security (Angel), crew welfare [61].

Financials

Private; revenue not disclosed. The company states it serves more than 600 shipping companies and 12,000 vessels [61]. Viasat received $203m of total proceeds for its minority interest, completed in its fiscal Q4 2026 (Jan–Mar 2026) [20,63].

8. Network Innovations

Ownership / HQ

Private; HQ Calgary, Alberta [21]. The controlling shareholder was not identified in the sources reviewed.

Operators

Starlink – Yes, authorized reseller [64]; OneWeb – Yes, distribution partner [35]; Viasat/Inmarsat – Inmarsat listed as a partner [65]; SES (incl. Intelsat) – Intelsat listed as a partner [65].

Sectors

Enterprise, energy, mining, utilities, government/defence, maritime, emergency response [65].

Capabilities

Systems design and integration, managed network services, field services, and the Argus secured networks offering [65].

Financials

Private; not disclosed. It completed the acquisition of Infosat (Canada and US) from Telesat, with final closings effective 31 Jul 2025 [21].

9. Tampnet

Ownership / HQ

Infrastructure-fund owned. 3i Infrastructure plc holds roughly 45–50% interests in the Tampnet group entities listed in its accounts. Operating company: Tampnet AS, Norway [66].

Operators

Starlink – Yes; OneWeb – Yes, as LEO layers on top of subsea fibre and 4G/5G [67]; Viasat/Inmarsat – not verified; SES – not verified.

Sectors

Offshore oil & gas (North Sea, Gulf of Mexico, Brazil), carbon capture, offshore vessels [67,66].

Capabilities

Subsea fibre, offshore 4G/5G LTE, line-of-sight radio, Versa SD-WAN with AI traffic orchestration, private 5G networks, a 24/7 NOC [67].

Financials

Group revenue and EBITDA are not published. 3iN valued its Tampnet holding at £434m at 31 Mar 2026 (31 Mar 2025: £379m) and reported EBITDA outperformance [66].

10. Space Norway (incl. former Telenor Satellite)

Ownership / HQ

State-owned: Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries [68]. Acquired Telenor Satellite, finalised in January 2024 [69].

Operators

Starlink – Yes, authorized reseller since 2 Jun 2025 [70]; OneWeb – offered via Telenor Maritime (a separate Telenor company) [71]; Viasat/Inmarsat – capacity partner, not reseller: its ASBM HEO system (in service since Nov 2024) supplies capacity to Viasat among others [68]; SES – not verified.

Sectors

Maritime, offshore, government/defence (Arctic), broadcasting.

Capabilities

THOR GEO fleet, ASBM Arctic HEO, VSAT platforms, combined GEO + Starlink managed services [70,68].

Financials

FY2025 group revenue NOK 1,357m and EBITDA NOK 718m (2024: NOK 2,195m revenue; 2024 included one-off ASBM income) [68].

11. Nelco (Tata Group)

Ownership / HQ

Public (listed in India), Tata Group. India.

Operators

OneWeb – Yes, distribution partner for India; commercial launch awaits regulatory and spectrum approvals [36]; Starlink – No (open to other LEO tie-ups, per report) [36]; Viasat/Inmarsat and SES – not verified.

Sectors

Satellite network services in India; reported as a single 'Network Systems' segment [72].

Capabilities

VSAT network operations and managed services in India (segment detail not broken out) [72].

Financials

FY2025-26 (to 31 Mar 2026), consolidated: income from operations Rs 30,660 lakh (≈ Rs 306.6 crore, +0.6%); PBITDA Rs 3,292 lakh; net profit Rs 332 lakh [72].

12. Telstra (telco channel exemplar)

Ownership / HQ

Public (ASX: TLS). Australia.

Operators

Starlink – Yes: resells Starlink home internet [73] and offers Satellite Messaging over Starlink Direct to Cell, extended to Enterprise on 11 Dec 2025 [74]; OneWeb – Yes: LEO cellular backhaul for more than 300 remote mobile sites (announced 12 Feb 2024) [75]; Viasat/Inmarsat and SES – not verified.

Sectors

Consumer, small business, enterprise, mobile backhaul.

Capabilities

National mobile network, satellite ground stations, bundling of Starlink with Telstra services [76].

Financials

FY26 (to 30 Jun 2026) total income A$23,405m (−0.9%) [76]. Satellite revenue is not broken out.

Telstra stands in for the telco channel (similar arrangements exist at other operators but were not verified for this report). Telcos give Starlink and OneWeb retail reach and regulatory cover, but take a thin margin.

13. Kymeta

Ownership / HQ

Private. HQ Redmond, Washington, US [77].

Operators

OneWeb – Yes, distribution partner [33] and multi-orbit defence offering [78,79]; Starlink, Viasat/Inmarsat, SES – not verified (GEO Ku bundles; operators not named).

Sectors

Government/defence, first responders, land mobility.

Capabilities

Flat-panel multi-orbit terminals (Osprey/Goshawk u8), a U.S. DoD bundle (Ku GEO + OneWeb LEO + TRANSEC + LTE) [77]; selected for the U.S. Army NGC2 pilot [77].

Financials

Private; revenue not disclosed. A $20m growth-capital facility from Trinity Capital is reported [80]; the date was not verified (page blocked).

Other notable channel players (not fully profiled). Anuvu (Platinum Equity, acquired Oct 2025 [23]) signed a Starlink maritime reseller agreement in 2023 [81] but sold its maritime, energy and government connectivity business to FMC GlobalSat in April 2024 [82]; it now focuses on aviation (and holds Eutelsat 10B capacity [16]). Tototheo Global signed a new OneWeb partner agreement [16], and a third-party report links it to Starlink's maritime unlimited package [83] (unverified). CDW, Insight and WWT are emerging Starlink enterprise channels in North America [30]. SES itself acts as a Eutelsat OneWeb distribution partner in aviation [16].

6. Assessment

Market leaders

In maritime and energy, Marlink (more than $800m stated revenue [3]) and Speedcast (Tier 1 Starlink, OneWeb GDP [7,8]) lead as independent integrators, with Navarino (12,000 vessels [61]) and KVH as strong second-tier players. In business aviation, Gogo/Satcom Direct is the main multi-operator channel. In commercial aviation, integrators (Panasonic, and SES/Intelsat as operator-integrator) matter more than resellers. Telcos (Telstra and others) are the scale channel for consumer and backhaul.

Multi-orbit strategy winners

Firms that own the integration layer (SD-WAN/edge orchestration, cybersecurity, field service) and can bond two LEO networks are best placed: Marlink's Sealink Multi-LEO [3], Speedcast's SIGMA [9], KVH ONE [11], and Tampnet's fibre + LEO [67]. OneWeb's partner-led model and SLAs (cited in Telstra's backhaul deal [75]) make it the natural second LEO layer next to Starlink. Viasat's NexusWave [39] and SES's Cruise mPOWERED + Starlink [19] show operators bundling multi-orbit themselves, which compresses reseller value in those segments.

Financial health and risks

Leverage. Gogo is at B2 with 4.4x pro-forma leverage [14]. Marlink carries term-loan B debt ($670m + €378m [6]). SES is at 4.4x against a ≤3.0x target [17]. EchoStar's balance sheet is dominated by spectrum-related impairments and debt [58]. KVH reported no interest expense for 2025 [51]. Nelco and Space Norway report positive EBITDA [72,68].

Starlink disintermediation. The reseller pause [15] and Starlink's direct enterprise teams [1] limit new entrants and could squeeze margins for incumbents when contracts are renegotiated. In aviation, Moody's cites Gogo losing the NetJets opportunity to Starlink [14]. The counter-trend is that SpaceX explicitly values channel partners for regulated markets and government [1,15].

Mix and margin. Hardware is shrinking and airtime is growing. KVH's product revenue fell 27% in FY2025 [51]. Resellers have to make up for thinner LEO airtime margins with managed services, cybersecurity and IT.

M&A outlook

Recent deals point to: (a) PE-to-PE and founder recapitalisations (Navarino–ICG [62]; Anuvu–Platinum [23]); (b) infrastructure carve-outs to infrastructure funds (Speedcast teleports to EQT's SatPort [9]); (c) defence-led bolt-ons (Marlink–GRC [22]); and (d) operator divestment of channel stakes (Viasat–Navarino [20]). Bloomberg's 2025 report that Speedcast was weighing separate auctions for its services, infrastructure and government businesses [49] implies further transactions are possible, including for UltiSat (speculative).

What to watch, 2026–2028

Whether Starlink reopens its reseller programme or formalises tiers after its IPO [15,31]; Amazon's LEO entry as a third LEO option for resellers (not researched in depth here); Eutelsat's IRIS² role and continued LEO growth [16]; SES deleveraging and its 9 Dec 2026 Capital Markets Day [17]; Viasat ViaSat-3 F3 entry into service and NexusWave growth [20]; Gogo's Galileo/5G ramp against Starlink [13]; Speedcast's post-carve-out strategy; and completion and integration of Marlink–GRC [22].

Caveats and data gaps

  • Private companies (Marlink, Speedcast, Navarino, Network Innovations, Tampnet, Kymeta) do not publish audited group financials. Marlink's '>$800m' is a company statement; Speedcast's ~$500m is a third-party estimate; Tampnet is shown via its owner's valuation.
  • Panasonic Avionics and Hughes figures are segment- or parent-level; Telstra's figure is group total income and not satellite-specific.
  • Operator relationships marked 'n.v.' (not verified) may exist but could not be confirmed from primary sources within this research. 'Hist.' marks a documented but possibly lapsed relationship.
  • Several sources returned HTTP 403/401 to automated checks (bot protection or paywall) but are legitimate and open in a browser; these are noted in the References. One link (Satcom Direct newsroom) returned 404 and was replaced; an Aviation Week article requiring login was dropped.
  • No FX conversions were made; figures are in reporting currency.
